fixer.title: The Architect of the Exit Ramp
fixer.subtitle: I show up with tools because I cannot stand watching you suffer.
fixer.content:
The meeting ended at six. You called me at six-fifteen, voice already fraying at the edges. And something in my chest tightened. That signal I've learned to recognize as do something, do something right now.

I pulled over. I grabbed a pen. I started running scenarios the way I always do: immediately, automatically, without deciding to.

Find the problem. Name it. Fix it. That's how you make it stop.

"Did you try talking to HR?" I asked. You went quiet. The kind of quiet that means I've already lost you. I won't realize that for another four minutes.

What I don't know how to explain is this: watching you spiral without trying to stop it feels like watching someone drown and choosing not to throw the rope. I'm not trying to minimize your pain. I'm trying to get you out of it. To me, those have always been the same act.

But we ended up fighting about my tone. Not your day. Not the actual problem. My tone. And somewhere between the parking lot and the driveway, I started wondering what I'm supposed to do with all this love I have nowhere to put.

feeler.title: The One Who Just Needed You to Stay
feeler.subtitle: I wasn't asking you to fix it. I was asking you to stay.
feeler.content:
I called from the parking lot because I needed to hear your voice. Just your voice. Not a plan.

You asked me three questions in thirty seconds. I counted, which is probably its own kind of problem.

This isn't a puzzle. It's just a bad day. Can we let it be a bad day together.

"Did you try talking to HR?" you asked. And something in me deflated. The way a balloon meets something pointed. Not from impact. Just from contact.

The thing you don't see is what your questions say to me. Not care. Urgency. Every solution tells me you want this conversation to be over. Every fix is a door with an exit sign above it. You're not wrong that HR might help. You're wrong about what I needed from you in that moment.

I don't want to be a problem with a solution. I want to be a person you're willing to sit with, even when there's no lever to pull, no progress to report, no resolution in sight.

The parking lot was cold. I was still in my car. I just wanted you to stay on the line a little longer.

bridge.prompt: The fight was never about what was said. It was about what was needed. Neither of you knew how to ask.
bridge.subtitle: You've heard one need. Are you ready to listen to the other?
